content.Title: Indications and contraindications for heart transplantation (table)
Indications: No other therapeutic option, except for LVAD as bridge to transplantation (BTT)
Contraindications: Severe peripheral arterial or cerebrovascular disease
Pharmacologic irreversible pulmonary hypertension (consider LVAD to reverse elevated pulmonary vascular resistance with subsequent re-evaluation to establish candidacy)
Malignancy with poor prognosis (collaborate with oncology to stratify risk of tumour progression or recurrence with immunosuppression)
Irreversible liver dysfunction (cirrhosis) or irreversible renal dysfunction (e.g., creatinine clearance <30 mL/min/1.73 m^2). Combined heart–liver or heart–kidney transplant may be considered
Other serious comorbidity with poor prognosis
Pre-transplant BMI >35 kg/m^2 (weight loss is recommended to achieve a BMI <35 kg/m^2)
Psychological instability that jeopardizes proper follow-up and intensive therapeutic regimen after heart transplantation
Insufficient social supports to achieve compliant care in the outpatient setting

Footnotes.a: Active infection is a relative contraindication to transplant although in some cases of infected LVADs it may actually be an indication.

content.Source: Adapted from Crespo-Leiro et al.; Table 17
